reason: Both answers push back, and both cover the liability cap, the narrowed IP indemnity and a data super-cap. Answer A puts the general cap first, gives a 12-month fee cap with a 2x fallback, and lists the standard uncapped carve-outs. It says to concede an uncapped IP indemnity once its scope is narrowed, and it states the bankruptcy asymmetry as a clear walk-away line. It also adds useful tactics: tying the cap to insurance limits, sending all redlines in one pass, and checking IP ownership. Answer B ranks the consequential damages waiver above the cap. Its "losing IP in bankruptcy" claim is loosely reasoned, and its suggestion to limit the indemnity to US patents is debatable. It is thinner on the main asymmetry argument. A is better.
